To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel sampling scheme that draws high-quality samples from the implicit energy-based model behind MLMs, and we show that the masked condition on their own do NOT yield a Markov Chain whose stationary distribution is the desired distribution.

(1) the masked conditionals do not yield a stationary distribution over the target sequence space; (2) the proposed sampling scheme based on Metropolis--Hasting algorithm is effective for sampling from the target distribution.

(1) MLMs are not energy-based models, and (2) we can construct an energy-based model that is trained in the same manner as an MLM and that can be used to draw samples that are better than those drawn using MLMs themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implicit energy networks underlying masked language models.
the question of how to sample from the energy-based sequence models that are trained by the MLM objective.
exposing the implicit energy network behind the masked language models and providing an efficient sampling scheme to draw samples from this network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MLMs do not specify a principled probabilistic distribution over sequences, but they can be used as an energy function to draw samples from a target distribution.

our work provides a new way of understanding the implicit energy networks behind the masked language models and proposes an effective sampling approach to draw samples from them, which is of both theoretical and practical interest.

our approach provides a principled sampling scheme for MLMs that is more efficient and more accurate than other recent approaches, and that it can serve as a foundation for future research in energy-based modeling of sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, we provide a new perspective to understand the implicit generative process behind masked language models and develop a tractable algorithm for sampling from the implicit energy networks of these models.
the masked language modeling is not a random walk on the sequence space, but an implicit energy function on the sequence space that is not easy to sample from.
we provide an energy parametrization for MLMs, and we develop a tractably efficient sampling algorithm for drawing samples from this model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MLMs are indeed capable of learning a probability distribution over the sequence space, and the proposed parametrization and sampling algorithm can be used as a general framework for generating high-quality samples from a wide variety of sequence models.

, despite the apparent simplicity of the MLM objective, the trained models are actually capable of specifying a rich distribution over the space sequences, and our work exposes the energy networks that underlie these models.

, despite the fact that MLMs are not designed to be energy-based models, they implicitly specify a tractable and effective parametrization of an energy function, which can be leveraged to draw high-quality samples.
